text:
Kiran CS: Heads-up — multiple customers escalated: 5xx + 30s timeouts on hosted inference /v1/generate over the last ~20m. Sample request IDs: rcq-9f4, rcq-9f8, rcq-9fa. Affected regions reported: us-west-2, eu-west-1. RL ticket #12345. Can SRE triage? :rotating_light:

Ema SRE: On it. Are we seeing any SLO burn alerts or console pages lighting up? :eyes:

incident-bot: ALERT: SLO violation detected — api.gateway.generate 5xx rate = 3.8% over 10m (threshold 1.0%). Incident ticket created: INC-1893002711.

Josh Observability: Looking at traces now. Sampling low but I can see a pattern — long queue wait time at gateway before the runtime accepts the connection. A bunch of traces point to runtime-host-4 as the common upstream. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/api-gateway-latency (open to eng team)

Mike Oncall: I repro locally with a quick script — about ~1/3 requests end in 504 after ~29s. Response headers show `x-runtime-host: runtime-host-4`, `x-proxy-retries: 1`, and sometimes `x-client-timeout`.

Mike Oncall (example curl):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.54.12.1) port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 52.54.12.1...
* Connection timed out after 30000 milliseconds
```

Tara Platform: Logs from proxy-nginx show a spike in `502: upstream prematurely closed connection` and `connection reset by peer` for runtime-host-4. Also seeing `connect() failed (111: Connection refused)` intermittently — suggests the runtime process or its accept queue is saturated.

Ema SRE: Potential mitigations: 1) temporarily route traffic away from runtime-host-4, 2) scale runtime pool (add replicas), 3) increase gateway upstream timeout as a short-term move, 4) raise sampling for traces to capture full path. Josh, can you confirm runtime-host-4 metrics (CPU/GPU/load)?

Josh Observability: runtime-host-4 GPU memory looks fine, but user CPU for the runtime process is at ~95% and loadavg is high. No OOM kills seen. Kernel shows high context switches and accept queue depth is rising. Query I ran:
```
# logs: proxy-nginx
jsonPayload.service="proxy-nginx" resource.labels.host="runtime-host-4" severity>="ERROR" | limit 50
```

Mike Oncall: I'm SSHing into k8s and will cordon + drain runtime-host-4 to force traffic redistribution and spin up a new replica. Commands:```
kubectl cordon node/runtime-host-4
kubectl drain node/runtime-host-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl scale deployment/runtime --replicas=6 -n redwood-runtime
```

Support Bot: Customer update sent: "We're investigating elevated errors/timeouts — interim mitigation in progress." Also noting several customers reported an auth 401 immediately prior to timeouts (they retried and then hit a 504). Could be client retry patterns amplifying pile-up.

Ema SRE: Good catch on the 401->retry pattern. That could be head-of-line blocking if retries flood the gateway. Also seeing a tracing gap: traces for some requests drop after gateway span — no child spans from runtime for ~8m window. Might be lost trace headers on retries or sampling. Josh, bump sampling for this route to capture more.

Josh Observability: Bumped sampling to 50% for `/v1/generate` route and added a temporary trace tag to track `x-request-id`. Added a log query to correlate:```
resource.type="k8s_container"
labels.k8s_container_name="proxy-nginx" jsonPayload.request_id=~"rcq-.*" | stats count() by jsonPayload.request_id, jsonPayload.status
```

Mike Oncall: Node cordoned + drained. New replica deployed. Traffic redistributed away from runtime-host-4. Error rate dropped from ~9% -> ~1.2% over the last 3m per dashboard. Continuing to monitor.

Kiran CS: Thanks — I'll update customers and close the RL ticket only once we confirm stability. Any follow-ups needed for postmortem?

Ema SRE: Postmortem checklist: collect runtime-host-4 logs (container and node), procsnapshot, kernel logs, Jaeger traces for the 20m window, config for proxy-nginx upstream timeouts, and customer request IDs. Also add a short-term runbook note about avoiding single-host hotspots for runtime pool.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1893002711 updated: status=monitoring, severity=sev2, start_ts=1893002711, last_update_ts=1893002805.

Mike Oncall: I'll keep eyes on the SLO dashboard for the next 1h and follow up here with any regression.

Kiran CS: Appreciated — will send customer follow-up that we've applied a mitigation and are collecting artifacts for a postmortem."
